arxiv-1504-01014.title: Discrete uncertainty principles and sparse signal processing
arxiv-1504-01014.creator: Afonso S. Bandeira, Megan E. Lewis, Dustin G. Mixon
arxiv-1504-01014.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Afonso S. Bandeira, Megan E. Lewis, Dustin G. Mixon. We develop new discrete uncertainty principles in terms of numerical sparsity, which is a continuous proxy for the 0 0 -norm. Unlike traditional sparsity, the continuity of numerical sparsity naturally accommodates functions which are nearly sparse. After studying these principles and the functions that achieve exact or near equality in them, we identify certain consequences in a number of sparse signal processing applications.

arxiv-2011-04907.creator: Paxton Turnerlabel=paxton]pax@mit.edu, Jingbo Liulabel=jingbo]jingbol@illinois.edu, and Philippe Rigollet label=rigollet]rigollet@math.mit.edu
arxiv-2011-04907.description: Abstract Coresets have emerged as a powerful tool to summarize data by selecting a small subset of the original observations while retaining most of its information. This approach has led to significant computational speedups but the performance of statistical procedures run on coresets is largely unexplored.

arxiv-2111-10532.title: Statistical ensembles for phase coexistence states specified by noncommutative additive observables
arxiv-2111-10532.creator: Yasushi Yoneta, Akira Shimizu
arxiv-2111-10532.description: Abstract A phase coexistence state cannot be specified uniquely by any intensive parameters, such as the temperature and the magnetic field, because they take the same values over all coexisting phases. It can be specified uniquely only by an appropriate set of additive observables.

arxiv-2304-12149.description: Abstract Deep learning has made great strides in medical imaging, enabled by hardware advances in GPUs. One major constraint for the development of new models has been the saturation of GPU memory resources during training. This is especially true in computational pathology, where images regularly contain more than 1 billion pixels.

arxiv-2407-07280.creator: Hideya Watanabe

arxiv-2409-09684.title: A natomy of Machines for Markowitz: Decision-Focused Learning for Mean-Variance Portfolio Optimization CCS: Computing methodologies Artificial intelligence
arxiv-2409-09684.creator: Junhyeong Lee, Inwoo Tae, Yongjae Lee
arxiv-2409-09684.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Junhyeong Lee, Inwoo Tae, Yongjae Lee. Markowitz laid the foundation of portfolio theory through the mean-variance optimization (MVO) framework. However, the effectiveness of MVO is contingent on the precise estimation of expected returns, variances, and covariances of asset returns, which are typically uncertain. Machine learning models are becoming useful in estimating uncertain parameters, and such models are trained to minimize prediction errors, such as mean squared errors (MSE), which treat prediction errors uniformly across assets.

arxiv-2410-15711.title: Quantiles and Quantile Regression on Riemannian Manifolds a measure-transportation-based approach
arxiv-2410-15711.creator: Marc Hallin, Hang Liu
arxiv-2410-15711.description: Abstract Increased attention has been given recently to the statistical analysis of variables with values on nonlinear manifolds. A natural but nontrivial problem in that context is the definition of quantile concepts. We are proposing a solution for compact Riemannian manifolds without boundaries; typical examples are polyspheres, hyperspheres, and toroïdal manifolds equipped with their Riemannian metrics.

arxiv-2602-09670.creator: Ilay Kamai, Marc-Huertas Company, Michael J. Smith, Hagai B. Perets
arxiv-2602-09670.description: Abstract Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) offer unique opportunities for scientific tasks, yet their ability to reason over complex numerical data remains largely unexplored. We propose a simple mechanism to introduce domain-specific physical knowledge into LLMs by fusing pre-trained latent physical features with a pre-trained language model.

pmc-12428541.title: Engineering of Humanized PSMA-Directed CAR T Cells for Potent and Specific Elimination of Prostate Cancer Cells
pmc-12428541.creator: Tobias D Deller, Jamal Alzubi, Laura Mosti, Marie Peschers, Christian Gratzke, Philipp Wolf, Toni Cathomen, Tabish H Khan, Naoshad Muhammad
pmc-12428541.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T cell therapy has achieved high response rates in patients with relapsed or refractory hematologic malignancies. However, comparable efficacy in solid tumors remains limited, partly due to poor CAR T cell persistence and immune-mediated rejection. A major contributor, which has hampered the clinical efficacy of CAR T cells in clinical practice, is the immunogenicity of the murine-derived single-chain variable fragments (scFvs) commonly used in CAR constructs.

pmc-12545147.title: Case Report: Immunophenotypically diverse immature patterns, including variable TdT expression, in aggressive B-cell lymphomas and leukemia with MYC rearrangement
pmc-12545147.creator: Daishi Kato, Takahiro Fujino, Reiko Isa, Haruya Okamoto, Taku Tsukamoto, Shinsuke Mizutani, Yuji Shimura, Tsutomu Kobayashi, Hitoji Uchiyama, Masafumi Taniwaki, Aya Miyagawa-Hayashino, Junya Kuroda
pmc-12545147.description: This study is a retrospective analysis of our case series and literature review of aggressive B-cell lymphomas with MYC rearrangements that show immunophenotypic immaturity, including expression of terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (TdT), weak or negative CD20, and the absence of surface membrane immunoglobulin (smIg) and light chains.

pmc-12561651.title: A Comparative Analysis of Sustainable Design Tools for Product Redesign Within a Business Context
pmc-12561651.creator: Sarah McInerney, Peter H Niewiarowski, Olga Speck, Richard Bonser
pmc-12561651.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In recent years, corporate perceptions of environmental sustainability have shifted from viewing it as a compliance burden to recognizing it as a strategic driver of innovation and competitive advantage, prompting a demand for effective sustainable design tools. Traditionally, tools like the Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) tool have been used to evaluate environmental impacts, yet their complexity, cost, and retrospective focus make them impractical for driving early-stage, disruptive innovation.

pmc-12644516.creator: Deng Zihan, Zhu Fuxian, Xu Xiaoli
pmc-12644516.description: As a way to guide and supervise public opinion, news inevitably contains certain emotional tendencies. Whether such emotional tendencies will have an impact on the entrepreneurial decisions and behaviors of micro-subjects has become an economic topic of great research value.

pmc-12748322.description: BackgroundCircadian dysregulation has been shown to be associated with the progression of pancreatic cancer (PC). pmc-13085040.description: IntroductionDiverticular disease is commonly seen among patients with cardiovascular diseases and is linked to adverse outcomes. pmc-13174883.title: The First Documented Case of Ectrodactyly in Ghana: A Case Report
pmc-13174883.creator: Schambach J Sobbin, Adjoa E Hackman, Frank E Gyamfi, Dennis K Kyeremeh, Joseph D Appiagyei, Fareeda Galley
pmc-13174883.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ectrodactyly, also called split-hand/foot malformation, is a rare congenital limb defect. We report what seems to be the first documented case of ectrodactyly in Ghana. A term female neonate, delivered by elective cesarean section at 38 weeks and 1 day to a 45-year-old multiparous mother with poorly controlled chronic hypertension and well‑controlled gestational diabetes, was found to have bilateral cleft‑type deformities of both hands and feet.
